verdicts.name: services/mech/progress_service.py:1458 ProgressService.release_gift

findings.trigger: Repeated real donations booked through add_donation() -> apply_power_event() -> apply_donation_units(), each individually valid (<= MAX_DONATION = $10,000, refused otherwise since B14). At line 882 'snap.cumulative_donations_cents += units_cents' runs with no ceiling check at all, unlike add_system_power() (lines 1017-1027) which caps the same field at MAX_CUMULATIVE ($1,000,000) before adding. And once the mech has reached level 11, apply_donation_units's own fast path (lines 884-886: 'if snap.level >= 11: snap.power_acc += units_cents; return') adds to power_acc with no MAX_POWER ($100,000) check either - and the capacity-based clamp that guards power_acc for levels 1-10 in apply_power_event (battery_capacity_cents) returns None at level 11, so it never fires there. Enough real donations therefore push cumulative_donations_cents and, once at level 11, power_acc past the ceilings the MAX_CUMULATIVE/MAX_POWER constants declare, with no warning and no refusal - only add_system_power (a separate, non-donor path) still enforces them.
findings.suggestion: Either apply the same MAX_POWER/MAX_CUMULATIVE bounds inside apply_donation_units (and in apply_power_event's post-processing for the level-11 case) that add_system_power already applies, or, if unlimited growth for a maxed-out mech's power/cumulative total is the intended 'immortal mech' behaviour (as battery_capacity_cents's docstring suggests for the level-11 case), remove or repurpose the now-orphaned MAX_POWER/MAX_CUMULATIVE constants and say so, so the two paths do not silently disagree.
findings.unsure_why: battery_capacity_cents's docstring explicitly says level 11 'has no goal and therefore no limit', which reads as a deliberate design choice for power_acc at max level; and B14's own text implies the old MAX_CUMULATIVE clamp inside the donation path was considered part of the problem it fixed ('quietly reshaped ... where nobody is told'), so leaving it out of apply_donation_units could be intentional rather than a leftover. I could not tell whether the still-enforced MAX_POWER/MAX_CUMULATIVE checks in add_system_power are the surviving, deliberate half of that decision or simply an inconsistency nobody revisited when add_donation's own cap (MAX_DONATION) was added.

findings.trigger: ProgressService.add_donation (and, the same way, add_system_donation at line ~1347) decides whether an idempotency_key was already booked by scanning read_events() (line 216), which silently drops any log line it cannot parse ('damaged' lines are skipped and only counted when a caller explicitly asks via count_damaged=True - rebuild_from_events is the only caller that does). If the event log line holding a donation with idempotency_key K becomes unreadable AFTER that donation was already fully applied to the snapshot (independent corruption of an already-committed line - bit rot, a manual edit, a partial read over the SMB-mounted data dir - as opposed to a line torn mid-write, which the snapshot also never picked up and whose retry is a legitimate first booking), a later request carrying the same key K finds no 'existing' entry, is treated as new, and is credited a second time even though the money was already recorded once.
findings.suggestion: Have the idempotency check use read_events(count_damaged=True) and, when damaged_lines > 0, refuse the booking (or fall back to consulting the snapshot's cumulative/last_event_seq) instead of silently proceeding as if the key had never been seen - mirroring the refusal rebuild_from_events already applies when it detects a damaged log for the same reason (state cannot be shown to be correct with missing lines).
findings.unsure_why: I could not tell how likely independent post-commit corruption of a single already-applied log line is in production versus the crash-mid-append case, which this code already handles correctly (that retry is a genuine first booking, not a double one). The distinction between 'line was never really written' and 'line was written, applied, and later corrupted' is invisible to read_events() and to me from the source alone.

notes: services/mech/gifts.py (grant_power_gift, release_gift) is referenced by ProgressService.power_gift/release_gift but was not included in source/, so those two names could not be reviewed - see their not_checked verdicts. Separately, the comment at progress_service.py line ~998-999 ('_snapshot_lags... stage 4 review, section 24 F1') documents that this exact section was reviewed before and a prior finding (snapshot lagging behind an appended power event) was already fixed via _heal_if_lagging; I confirmed that mechanism looks sound and did not re-report it. I have deliberately used 'F1'/'F2' as this report's own finding ids per TASK.md's template, unrelated to the F1 named in that comment.
